dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of television viewers zapping behaviour commercial allocation and advertisement markets kyan and inoue 2013

description: This 2013 preprint proposes a simple probabilistic agent-based model of how television viewers switch channels, presented as a theoretical platform for studying collective human behaviour at the macroscopic scale from decisions at the microscopic scale. Each viewer chooses a station using three factors: physical constraints on television controllers, exogenous information such as a station's programme advertising, and endogenous word-of-mouth information. The stochastic process of audience measurements, such as programme rating point and gross rating point, is reconstructed from these decisions, and the model is extended to commercial allocation and advertisement markets. Producer: Hiroyuki Kyan and Jun-ichi Inoue, arXiv, 19 September 2013. Coverage: abstract population of viewers, no specific market. Access: paper on arXiv; no code or dataset link was read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the model is simple and stylised and has not been calibrated to a broadcasting market in the material read here. Simulation uses: it can be reused to study audience shifts and demand for broadcast services, for example after a switch-off or outage of a station. Related records: none linked.
